ConfirmClearHistory: Clear every recorded run? This cannot be undone.
ConfirmDeleteScript: Delete "{0}"? This saves right away. Unsaved edits to other scripts stay unsaved.
ConfirmImportReplacingMany: {0} will replace a script with the same ID: {1}.
ConfirmImportReplacingOne: 1 will replace a script with the same ID: {0}.
ConfirmImportReview: Imported scripts start disabled so you can review their steps, then save. Secret values are not in the file, so enter them again.
ConfirmNewAddress: Make a new webhook address? Anything still calling the old one stops working once you save.
EmptyConditions: No conditions. The script runs on every trigger that passes its filters.
EmptyScripts: No scripts yet. Select New to add one, or Import a file.
EmptySteps: No steps yet. Add one below.
ErrorDeleteRefused: The server refused to delete the script.
ErrorImportEmpty: That file has no scripts in it.
ErrorImportJson: That file is not valid JSON.
ErrorNoScriptsToExport: There are no scripts to export.
ErrorRunFailed: Could not start the script. Save it and try again.
ErrorSaveFirst: Save first: Run now runs the saved script.
ErrorSaveRefused: The server refused the save. Check each script and try again.
ErrorScriptAndTriggerRequired: A script and a trigger are required.
ErrorScriptNotSaved: No saved script has this ID. Save the script first.
ErrorSecretName: Use capital letters, digits, and underscores.
ErrorTestFailed: The test could not run. Check the steps and try again.
ErrorTooManyRuns: Too many runs are waiting. Try again in a moment.
HeaderSaveOutput: Save the output for later steps
HeaderSaveResponse: Save the response for later steps
HelpAllConditions: Run only when every condition matches.
HelpAnyCondition: Run when at least one condition matches.
HelpAppendFile: A full path whose folder exists. The file is created if missing.
HelpArguments: Each line is passed as one argument, with placeholders filled. Spaces and quotes in a value never split it.
HelpCommand: A path to a script or program, or a name on the server's PATH such as curl. The server must be able to reach the path. In Docker, mount it into the container and use the path inside it.
HelpContinueOnError: Run the following steps even if this one fails.
HelpCooldown: After a run, skip this script for the same trigger, user, and item until this long passes. 0 turns it off.
HelpDefaultTimeout: A command step that sets no timeout of its own is stopped after this long.
HelpEventItemForUser: Acts on the event's item for the event's user.
HelpForEach: A schedule, a webhook, and Run now have no item or user of their own. Running for each gives the steps one: every library item of the script's item kinds, or every user, that passes its conditions. A trigger that already has one runs once as usual.
HelpForEachLimit: Stops after this many matches. Each one is its own run in the history.
HelpFullRefresh: Fetch everything again rather than only what is missing.
HelpHistory: The most recent runs, newest first, including test runs. Click a run to see each step, its output, and the variables it received. Runs started by another script's Run another script step are listed too. Settings sets how many runs are kept.
HelpHistorySize: The oldest runs are dropped past this many. 0 keeps none.
HelpItemKinds: Run only for items of these kinds. Leave empty for every kind. Triggers without an item ignore this.
HelpOnFailure: That script gets the same event plus {0}, {1}, and {2}. It must be enabled, and needs no triggers of its own.
HelpPausePlayback: Pauses playback on the session that raised the event.
HelpPausedFor: Runs once per pause, after the session has stayed paused this long.
HelpPlayingFor: Runs once per playback, after this much playing time. Pauses do not count.
HelpPreset: Fills the fields below for a common service. Replace the URL and put tokens in the script's secrets.
HelpProgressPercent: Runs once per playback, when it goes from below this percentage to at or past it.
HelpRetries: Tries again after no answer, a 5xx, or a 429, waiting longer each time. Up to 5.
HelpRunDirectly: Starts one program with its arguments. Event values fill arguments safely.
HelpRunScript: Runs that script's steps with this event, skipping its triggers and filters. Scripts may run each other up to 3 levels deep.
HelpRunsAtOnce: How many scripts may run at the same time. Further runs wait their turn.
HelpSaveOutput: Later steps use it as {0}, and {1} holds the exit code.
HelpSaveResponse: Later steps use it as {0}, and {1} holds the HTTP status.
HelpScanLibraries: Queues a scan of every library, the same as the Scan All Libraries button.
HelpSchedule: A script on a schedule runs as a Jellyfin scheduled task. Once you save, it is listed under {0} in the {1} section, under this script's name and description. Set when it runs there, or run it by hand. It only runs on its schedule while the script is enabled.
HelpScriptDescription: What the script is for. Shown with its scheduled task when it runs on a schedule.
HelpScripts: A script runs its steps when one of its triggers happens. Item kinds, users, and conditions narrow which events it runs for. Steps can message or control sessions, change items and users, call webhooks, queue server tasks, or run a command at any path the server can reach.
HelpSecrets: Tokens and passwords this script uses. Use one as {0} in a step, or {1} in a command. Values are encrypted on the server, never shown again, left out of exports, and masked wherever they appear in the history.
HelpSetUserDisabled: Acts on the event's user. Administrators are never disabled.
HelpShellLine: Placeholders are not filled here, so event values cannot inject shell syntax. Read them from the environment, such as "$JF_ITEM_NAME". On Windows the line runs through cmd /c, which expands %JF_...% before parsing it, so there read event values inside a script file instead.
HelpSignOutUser: Signs the event's user out of every device. Administrators are never signed out.
HelpStepCondition: Tests any variable, such as ITEM_KIND, a webhook field, or one an earlier step saved. A step whose condition does not match is skipped, and the run carries on.
HelpStepTimeout: The command is stopped after this long. 0 uses the default from Settings.
HelpSteps: Run in order. Drag a step or use the arrows to move it. A failed step stops the rest unless it continues on error. Text fields accept {0} placeholders, listed under Variables. A step can have its own condition, and a command or HTTP request can save its output for the steps after it.
HelpStopScript: Ends the run here: the steps after this one are skipped, and the run still counts as succeeded. Give it a condition below so it only stops when you want it to.
HelpStreamCount: Runs when the number of active streams rises to this many. The event is the stream that reached it.
HelpTestAndRun: Test runs this script's steps now with sample values for the chosen trigger, including unsaved edits. Filters and conditions are not applied, and steps that act on a session, item, or user are skipped because the sample has none. Run now runs the saved script for real, whatever its triggers, filters, and cooldown say.
HelpThroughShell: One line for /bin/sh, for pipes and redirects. Event values come from the environment.
HelpTranscodeCount: Runs when the number of transcoding streams rises to this many. The event is the stream that reached it.
HelpTriggers: The script runs when any checked trigger happens. Search to narrow the list.
HelpUsers: Run only for these users. Leave all unchecked for everyone. On playback, any of the session's users counts. Triggers without a user ignore this.
HelpVariables: A command receives each of these as an environment variable, such as {0}, plus {1} with all of them. In a step's text fields, use {2}, {3} inside a JSON string, or {4} in a URL. Select one to copy it.
HelpWebhookAddress: Send a {0} here with a Jellyfin API key from Dashboard, API Keys. The address picks the script and the key proves the caller may run it. A request with either one missing is refused. Query parameters and JSON fields arrive as {1}.
HelpWorkingFolder: Optional. Defaults to the folder holding the script.
InfoCommandPaths: A {0} step runs a file at any path the server can reach. In Docker that is the path inside the container, so mount your scripts folder (for example {1}) and use {2}. The official image has a shell but no Python or most other interpreters, so a script should use {3} or an interpreter you mount or install yourself.
PathCheckFailed: The server could not check this path. {0}
PathExecutable: The server can see this file and it is executable.
PathFileMissing: The server cannot find this file. In Docker, mount it into the container.
PathIsFolder: This is a folder, not a file.
PathNotExecutable: The server can see this file, but it is not executable. Run chmod +x on it, or call it through an interpreter.
PathVisible: The server can see this file.
PlaceholderConditionValue: Type a value and press Enter
PlaceholderItemKinds: Any kind. Type to add one, such as Movie or Episode
PlaceholderJsonField: Everything, or a JSON field: data.items[0].name
PlaceholderNewName: Named after the template when left blank
ScheduleStartDaily: Until you change it there, the task starts out running every day at {0}.
ScheduleStartDays: Until you change it there, the task starts out running on {0} at {1}.
ScheduleStartInterval: Until you change it there, the task starts out running every {0} minutes.
ScheduleStartMonthly: The task starts with no schedule of its own. Add one under Scheduled Tasks.
StatusDuplicated: Duplicated as a disabled copy. Secrets are not copied.
StatusExportedMany: Exported {0} scripts. Secret values and webhook addresses are left out.
StatusExportedManyUnsaved: Exported {0} scripts, including unsaved edits. Secret values and webhook addresses are left out.
StatusExportedOne: Exported 1 script. Secret values and webhook addresses are left out.
StatusExportedOneUnsaved: Exported 1 script, including unsaved edits. Secret values and webhook addresses are left out.
StatusImported: Imported {0}. They are disabled and not saved yet: review each one, enable it, and click Save.
StatusRunStarted: Started. The result is on the History tab.
StatusStartedFromTemplate: Started from "{0}". Review it and click Save.
SummaryStopScript: Skip the steps after this one
TargetEventSession: The session that raised the event
TargetUserSessions: Every session of the event's users
TemplateAdminFailedTask: Message administrators when a task fails
TemplateCheckThenNotify: Call a service, then message administrators if it is down
TemplateCommandNewUser: Run a script when a user is created
TemplateDiscordNewMedia: Post new movies and episodes to Discord
TemplateHomeAssistantLights: Dim Home Assistant lights when playback starts
TemplateLogPlayback: Log every playback to a file
TemplateNtfyFailedSignin: Send a ntfy alert on a failed sign in
TemplateRemoteTranscode: Stop transcoding outside the home network
TemplateRestartWarning: Warn everyone when a restart is needed
TemplateStillWatching: Ask "Still watching?" after 3 hours of playback
TemplateTagUnwatched: Tag movies nobody has watched in 90 days
TemplateWebhookScan: Scan libraries when another service calls a webhook
TemplateWelcome: Greet users when their client connects
TestRunningNoTrigger: Running with sample values for the trigger…
TitleExportScripts: Export every script to a file
TitleNewAddress: The old address stops working once you save.
TriggerActivityLoggedDescription: Any entry is written to the activity log, by Jellyfin or another plugin.
TriggerAuthenticationFailureDescription: A sign in fails for an existing user.
TriggerClientConnectedDescription: A client opens its live connection, so it can receive messages and commands.
TriggerDeviceSettingsChangedDescription: A device's settings, such as its custom name, change.
TriggerFavoriteChangedDescription: A user adds or removes a favorite. IS_FAVORITE says which.
TriggerItemAddedDescription: An item arrives in a library, once its metadata is in.
TriggerItemAddedToCollectionDescription: An item is added to a collection.
TriggerItemRemovedFromCollectionDescript: An item is removed from a collection.
TriggerItemUpdatedDescription: An item's metadata or images change. Busy during scans.
TriggerLyricDownloadFailedDescription: A lyrics provider fails to download lyrics.
TriggerManualDescription: An administrator runs the script from the dashboard.
TriggerMarkedPlayedDescription: A user marks an item played.
TriggerMarkedUnplayedDescription: A user marks an item unplayed.
TriggerMetadataRefreshCompletedDescripti: A metadata refresh of an item finishes.
TriggerMetadataRefreshStartedDescription: A metadata refresh of an item starts.
TriggerNetworkChangedDescription: The server's network interfaces or addresses change.
TriggerNewDeviceSeenDescription: A device the server has not seen before starts a session.
TriggerPendingRestartDescription: The server needs a restart to apply a change.
TriggerPlaybackPausedForDescription: A client stays paused for the minutes you set, once per pause.
TriggerPlaybackPlayingForDescription: A client plays for the minutes you set, not counting pauses, once per playback.
TriggerPlaybackProgressReachedDescriptio: Playback passes the percentage you set, once per playback.
TriggerRecordingCancelledDescription: A scheduled Live TV recording is cancelled.
TriggerRecordingScheduledDescription: A Live TV recording is scheduled.
TriggerScheduleDescription: Runs as a Jellyfin scheduled task named after the script. Set when under Dashboard, Scheduled Tasks.
TriggerSeriesRecordingCancelledDescripti: A Live TV series recording is cancelled.
TriggerSeriesRecordingScheduledDescripti: A Live TV series recording is scheduled.
TriggerSessionStartedDescription: A client connects and starts a session.
TriggerStreamCountReachedDescription: The number of active streams rises to the number you set. The event is the stream that reached it.
TriggerSubtitleDownloadFailedDescription: A subtitle provider fails to download subtitles.
TriggerSwitchedToTranscodeDescription: A stream that was playing directly starts transcoding.
TriggerTaskCompletedDescription: A scheduled task finishes, whatever its outcome.
TriggerTranscodeCountReachedDescription: The number of transcoding streams rises to the number you set. The event is the stream that reached it.
TriggerUserLockedOutDescription: A user is locked out after too many failed sign ins.
TriggerUserUpdatedDescription: A user's name or profile is edited. Jellyfin does not report permission changes.
TriggerWebhookDescription: Another service calls the script's own address with a Jellyfin API key.
ValidateCooldown: "{0}": the cooldown must be between 0 and 86400 seconds.
ValidateForEachKinds: "{0}": running for each library item needs at least one item kind.
ValidateForEachLimit: "{0}": the most runs per event must be between 1 and 500.
ValidatePausedFor: "{0}": paused for must be between 1 and 1440 minutes.
ValidatePercentage: "{0}": the playback percentage must be between 1 and 99.
ValidatePlayingFor: "{0}": playing for must be between 1 and 1440 minutes.
ValidateSecretNames: "{0}": secret names use capital letters, digits, and underscores.
ValidateStepConditionName: "{0}": step {1} has a condition on something that is not a variable name.
ValidateStepConditionNumber: "{0}": step {1} has a condition that needs a number.
ValidateStepFile: "{0}": step {1} needs a full file path.
ValidateStepOutputName: "{0}": step {1} saves its output under a name of capital letters, digits, and underscores.
ValidateStepOutputTaken: "{0}": step {1} saves its output as {2}, which step {3} already uses.
ValidateStepRetries: "{0}": step {1} retries must be between 0 and 5.
ValidateStepScript: "{0}": step {1} needs a script to run.
ValidateStepShowFor: "{0}": step {1} show-for time must be between 0 and 300 seconds.
ValidateStepTimeout: "{0}": step {1} timeout must be between 0 and 3600 seconds.
ValidateStepUrl: "{0}": step {1} needs a URL that starts with http:// or https://.
ValidateStepWait: "{0}": step {1} must wait between 1 and 3600 seconds.
ValidateStreamCount: "{0}": the stream count must be between 1 and 100.
ValidateTranscodeCount: "{0}": the transcode count must be between 1 and 100.
VariableActiveStreams: How many sessions are playing something, counting this one.
VariableActiveTranscodes: How many sessions are transcoding, counting this one.
VariableActivitySeverity: Information, Warning, Error, and so on.
VariableActivityType: The entry's type, such as VideoPlayback or SessionStarted.
VariableArtist: The artists, comma separated, for audio.
VariableAudioCodec: The audio codec sent to the client, when transcoding.
VariableClient: The client application, such as Jellyfin Web.
VariableDateAdded: When the item was added, in UTC (ISO 8601).
VariableDayOfWeek: The server's local day of the week, such as Monday.
VariableDaysSinceActive: How many days ago the user was last active. Absent for a user who never was.
VariableDaysSinceAdded: How many days ago the item was added.
VariableDaysSincePlayed: How many days ago anyone last played the item, or it was added when nobody has.
VariableEpisodeNumber: The episode number, or a track number for audio.
VariableEvent: The trigger that ran the script, such as PlaybackStart.
VariableEventJson: Every other variable as one JSON object (environment only).
VariableFailedCount: How many runs failed, when the script ran for each item or user.
VariableFailedStep: The number of the step that failed.
VariableHasSubtitles: true when the item has subtitles, otherwise false. Video only.
VariableIsAdmin: true when the user is an administrator, otherwise false.
VariableIsDisabled: true when the user is disabled, otherwise false.
VariableIsFavorite: true when the item is now a favorite, otherwise false.
VariableIsLocal: true when the client is inside the local network, otherwise false.
VariableIsLocalWebhookVars: true when the caller is inside the local network, otherwise false.
VariableIsPaused: true when playback is paused, otherwise false.
VariableIsPlayed: true when the item is now played, otherwise false.
VariableItemKind: The item's kind, such as Movie or Episode.
VariableItemPath: The item's file or folder path.
VariableLibraryId: The ID of the library holding the item.
VariableLibraryName: The name of the library holding the item.
VariableOfficialRating: The parental rating, such as PG-13.
VariablePausedSeconds: How long the session has been paused, in seconds.
VariablePlayCount: How many times the user has played the item.
VariablePlayMethod: DirectPlay, DirectStream, or Transcode. On stop, the method seen while playing.
VariablePlayedByAnyone: true when any user has played the item, otherwise false.
VariablePlayedToCompletion: true when playback reached the end, otherwise false.
VariablePlayingSeconds: How long the session has played, not counting pauses, in seconds.
VariableProgramId: The program's ID, when it is known.
VariableProgressPercent: The playback position as a percentage of the runtime.
VariableSeasonNumber: The season number, for an episode.
VariableSeriesName: The series, for an episode or season.
VariableSettingsKey: Which settings changed, such as encoding or network. Empty for the main settings.
VariableTaskDurationSeconds: How long the task ran, in seconds.
VariableTaskError: The error message, when the task failed.
VariableTimestamp: When the event happened, in UTC (ISO 8601).
VariableTranscodeReasons: Why the server is transcoding, comma separated.
VariableUpdateReason: Why the item changed: MetadataImport, ImageUpdate, MetadataDownload, or MetadataEdit.
VariableUserIdActivity: The ID of the user the entry is about, when it has one.
VariableUserIdAuthFailure: The ID of the matching user.
VariableVideoCodec: The video codec sent to the client, when transcoding.
VariableWebhookBody: The request body as it was sent.
WarnCommandsTrusted: Commands run on the server as the account Jellyfin runs under. Only add commands you trust.
WarnConditionNeverAll: Never matches for {0}, so with "all conditions" the script will not run on those.
WarnConditionNoTrigger: None of the selected triggers supply this value, so this condition never matches.
WarnForEachItemsAlready: Every selected trigger already has an item, so the script runs once per event. Running for each applies to triggers such as On a schedule, Webhook received, and Run now.
WarnForEachNoKinds: Choose at least one item kind above, such as Movie, so the script knows which items to go through.
WarnForEachUsersAlready: Every selected trigger already has a user, so the script runs once per event. Running for each applies to triggers such as On a schedule, Webhook received, and Run now.
WarnNoItemKinds: With no item kinds, {0} runs for every kind a scan touches, including people, genres, studios, and folders.
WarnStepSkippedItemMany: Skipped for {0}, which have no item.
WarnStepSkippedItemOne: Skipped for {0}, which has no item.
WarnStepSkippedSessionMany: Skipped for {0}, which have no session.
WarnStepSkippedSessionOne: Skipped for {0}, which has no session.
WarnStepSkippedUserItemMany: Skipped for {0}, which have no user and item.
WarnStepSkippedUserItemOne: Skipped for {0}, which has no user and item.
WarnStepSkippedUserMany: Skipped for {0}, which have no user.
WarnStepSkippedUserOne: Skipped for {0}, which has no user.
WarnUsersIgnoredMany: Ignored for {0}, which have no user. The script runs on those events whatever these users do.
WarnUsersIgnoredOne: Ignored for {0}, which has no user. The script runs on that event whatever these users do.
